chapter_title: The Chapter of the Elements that wept

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
A sufficient complement of operative powers invested with external truths underwent a full series of grief in the ultimate degree three times, and then came into restraint and waiting. Yet there remains a final grief at the consummation, after which their lamentation in the ultimate degree ceases, because their work there is finished and no such distress can return.

The first grief came when those external truths first perceived active falsity, and saw it about to break forth against their domain. From that perception they comprehended the whole sequence of what would befall them. They recognized the evil that would be raised up to assault them, and yet by the necessity of order they were brought into direct engagement with it and contended against it. They prevailed over it and held it in restraint. They fixed it in the ultimate degree through the very forms and powers by which they act there, and so they subdued the intention of spiritual death, the ardor of self-love, and the obscurity of falsity that accompanied it.

The second grief came when the first good that had been set for combat was elevated from the ultimate obscurity and withdrawn upward, and those external truths were left in the lower state; this was the state in which their outward investment was removed and they were left to remain in what is beneath. When they perceived that the leading good had been raised out of ultimate falsity and had left them behind, and that they were abandoned amid hostility, they fell into grief and interior pain. Yet they could do nothing but endure, because their willing was turned toward every permitted suffering for the sake of the whole work. Therefore they remained behind and languished under the pressure of the heavy burden of all effects and labors required in the lowest degree, even until the final time.

The third grief came when the operation of Divine truth from the Divine removed a full series of outward powers of action, and arranged them beneath all things in the ultimate plane for service there. It gave them assurance and urging to elevate their understanding and to be raised into higher states from that low condition, and to progress through every lower degree of life until they should come to tranquility and peace, the rest prepared for them. When they perceived that this higher operation had separated itself from their immediate state while they themselves still remained below and had not yet been elevated, then those outward powers of action fell into grief. After that lamentation, they turned their intention toward all the higher states still hidden from them, and they became of one understanding and purpose: that they would be lifted into higher states and advance beyond all lower things, until the time appointed for their full elevation at the close of the ages.

The fourth grief will occur at the last judgment, when the final collective form of what has been gathered for elevation is taken up into complete separation from the lower. Then there will be lamentation on account of those who have confirmed falsity and profaned truth, because they can no longer receive restoration, since the operative powers by which conjunction could have been effected have been torn away from the influence of falsity. Those same souls, when that collected form is elevated and they are left alone, will lament because they remain behind in distress forever. For they are cut off and separated from that final collective, and it is necessary that those who have made themselves ready for ruin be taken into their recompense according to their deeds. They enter into falsity and are held in it, because they desired it and loved it, and placed their inmost delight and confidence within it. At the moment of the final elevation, they lament; and then their lamentation becomes vehement, because they are severed from the fellowship of that great collected form. They remain behind forever. This lamentation is dreadful and public among those fixed for ruin according to their works, and it does not cease, because they will not attain rest from that time onward.

For these external truths are also the outward investments of the fundamental evils and falsities in the ultimate degree, and this last lamentation rends them more than the three earlier griefs. It is worse than the former states, because this final lamentation is not for their own elevation, but for those souls who are cut off from peace, since no rest can come to relieve them from torment to eternity.

paragraph_translations.translation: A sufficient complement of operative powers invested with external truths went through bitter grief in the ultimate degree three times, and then came into restraint. Yet there remains a fourth grief at the consummation; after it, their lamentation can cease, and no such weeping will ever return.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: establishes the sequence of states and the final cessation of grief.

paragraph_translations.translation: The first grief arose when those external truths perceived active falsity and the hostile force about to break forth against their domain. From that perception they understood the whole course of what would happen to them. They knew the evil that would rise to assault them, yet by the necessity of order they were brought into direct engagement and fought against it. They prevailed and held it in restraint. They fixed it in the ultimate degree through the very forms and powers by which they act there, and so they overcame the intention of spiritual death, the ardor of self-love, and the obscurity of falsity.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: explains the first grief as perception of falsity and compelled combat ending in restraint.

paragraph_translations.translation: The second grief arose when the first good that had been set for combat was raised out of ultimate obscurity and withdrawn upward, leaving those external truths behind in what is beneath; this was the state in which their outward investment was removed and they were left in the lower degree. When they perceived that the leading good had been elevated from the ultimate falsity and had left them behind, and that they were abandoned amid hostility, they fell into grief and interior pain. Yet they could do nothing but endure, because their willing was turned toward accepting every permitted affliction for the sake of the whole work. Therefore they remained behind and languished under the pressure of the heavy burden of all effects and labors in the lowest degree, even until the final time.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: shifts from combat to separation, endurance, and prolonged burden in ultimates.
paragraph_translations.notes: The source text’s physical imagery of being stripped and left below is rendered as removal of outward investment and remaining in the lowest degree.

paragraph_translations.translation: The third grief arose when the operation of Divine truth from the Divine removed a full series of outward powers of action and arranged them beneath all things in the ultimate plane for service. It gave them assurance and urging to elevate their understanding and to be raised into higher states from that low condition, and to progress through every lower degree until they should reach tranquility and peace, the rest prepared for them. When they perceived that this higher operation had separated itself from their immediate state while they themselves remained behind and had not yet been elevated, then those outward powers of action grieved. After their lamentation, they turned their intention toward the higher states that were still hidden from them and became of one understanding and purpose: that they would be lifted into higher states and pass beyond all lower things until the time appointed for their full gathering and elevation at the close of the ages.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: introduces an ordering in ultimates and a promised ascent, producing grief and then unified resolve.
paragraph_translations.notes: The “sign” functions as assurance/urging; “journey through all the earths” is treated as progression through lower degrees.

paragraph_translations.translation: The fourth grief will come at the last judgment, when the final collective form of what has been gathered for elevation is taken up. Then there will be lamentation for those who have made falsity their truth and profaned what is holy, because no help can be given them: the operative powers by which conjunction could have been effected have been severed from the influence of falsity. Those souls also, when that collected form is elevated and they are left alone, will weep because they remain behind in affliction forever, cut off and separated from that final collective. It is necessary that those ready for ruin be brought into their recompense according to the deeds they have done. They enter into falsity and are bound within it, because they desired it and loved it and placed their inmost treasure in it. At the very moment of the final elevation they lament, and then cry out vehemently because they are severed from the fellowship of that great collected form; thus they remain behind forever. This great lamentation is terrible and occurs openly among those powers and souls fixed for ruin according to their works; it will not fall silent, because they will not attain rest from that time onward.
paragraph_translations.connection: SHIFTS: moves from the powers’ own process to the final judgment and the irreversible state of the profane.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Statue” is taken as a collective final form gathered for elevation; exact nuance is uncertain beyond its function as what is taken up at the end.

paragraph_translations.translation: Thus these same external truths are also the outward investments through which the fundamental evils and falsities work in the ultimate degree. This fourth grief tears them more than the former griefs and is far worse than the earlier states, because in this last lamentation they do not grieve for themselves but are heartsore for those souls cut off from peace, since no rest can ever come to them to relieve their torment.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: explains why the final grief is severer and directs it toward compassion for the lost.
paragraph_translations.notes: The phrase about “elements” is absorbed as “fundamental evils and falsities” operating in ultimates.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent as a single spiritual sequence: three earlier griefs mark perception of falsity, separation and endurance in ultimates, and ordered service with hope of elevation; the fourth grief shifts to final judgment and irreversible separation, culminating in unceasing lamentation for the profane. The only strain is the precise force of the “Statue,” which still functions consistently as a final gathered collective taken up at the consummation.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential framing of a fourfold sequence of states (three present griefs + one eschatological grief) with a functional reason for cessation. No narrative break; this paragraph supplies the chapter’s governing structure that the rest fulfills.
findings.evidence: Text: “wept bitterly three times… There is a fourth time of weeping… at the end… And then their crying can stop.” The spiritual reading reports no stumble here and treats it as “establishes the sequence of states and the final cessation of grief,” which matches a functional/state-based pedagogy rather than a jurisdictional list.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential combat scene: perception → necessary engagement → restraint/binding → named effects (death/fire/darkness) as functional qualities. No administrative intrusion (no ranks, stations, or inventories).
findings.evidence: Text: “had seen the darkness… by necessity they hastened to him and fought… They bound him with their body and their limbs.” The reading smoothly maps these as functional states (“perceived… compelled combat… held it in restraint”) and can justify correspondences from action (seeing, fighting, binding), not from who governs whom.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential separation-and-burden sequence. The physical ‘stripping’ imagery is continuous with the functional narrative (withdrawal of the First Man; the garments left below; endurance under ‘weighty burden’). Damage markers exist, but they do not force a voice shift or suggest insertion.
findings.evidence: Text: “their father… ascended… left them behind… stripped [them off]… they remained behind and grew sick under the pressure of the weighty burden.” The reading notes only a rendering choice (“physical imagery… rendered as removal of outward investment”)—not a narrative stumble. No named officials/territories appear.

findings.diagnosis: Mostly clean correspondential teaching, but with a localized lexical/imagistic strain that likely reflects either translation tradition or doctrinal accommodation rather than an administrative insertion. The sequence remains functional (stripping/placing beneath all things → sign → ascent/journey → ordained time).
findings.evidence: Text: “Living Spirit stripped off the three garments of activity, placing them beneath all things. He gave them a sign… journey through all the earths… reach the land of tranquility… time that was ordained.” The spiritual reading’s only pressure point is interpretive (“‘sign’ functions as assurance/urging; ‘journey through all the earths’… progression through lower degrees”). That is a normal correspondential ambiguity, not a governance list or seam-expansion.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty concentrated in the term ‘Statue’ and the sudden widening from the garments’ own process to a public eschatological tribunal. However, the passage is not administrative in Mani’s sense (no jurisdictional rosters; no ranked authorities; no stations/watches). It remains a state/process description of irreversible separation and recompense. The ‘shift’ is thematic, not a textual seam requiring excision.
findings.evidence: Text: “when the Statue will be taken up on the last day… weep for the souls… no help… limbs have been severed… This great weeping [before the rulers] is terrible.” The spiritual reading flags the only real stumble: “The only strain is the precise force of the ‘Statue’,” and notes a shift to final judgment. But even “before the rulers” functions as scene-setting for judgment, not an inserted administrative inventory (no names, no territorial assignments, no chain-of-command exposition). Removing it would collapse the promised ‘fourth weeping’ announced in ¶2.

findings.diagnosis: Clean closing rationale that ties the ‘elements/garments’ back to the fourfold weeping structure and clarifies the fourth grief’s object (for the lost, not themselves). This resolves rather than disrupts the chapter’s narrative.
findings.evidence: Text: “they too are the garments of these elements… This fourth time the weeping is not for themselves. Rather they weep… for these souls… cut off from peace.” The spiritual reading reports coherence and uses this to explain severity; no new administrative material is introduced.

textual_criticism.summary: No clear Mani-layer administrative insertions detected. The chapter reads as a coherent correspondential substrate organized by a fourfold sequence of states (¶2–¶7). The only substantive stumble noted by the spiritual reading is the referent of ‘the Statue’ in ¶6 and a thematic shift into eschatological judgment; this is best classified as genuine difficulty / mixed imagery rather than an administrative overlay or seam-expansion. Recommended actions: excise 0, annotate 0, none 6.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: The garments, the sons of the First Man, wept bitterly three times. Then they were silent. There is a fourth time of weeping, for they will weep at the end. And then their crying can stop, and they will never again weep from this time on.

Now, the first time of their weeping is when they had seen the darkness, the enemy being about to burst out against them. They understood everything that would happen to them. They were aware of the one that would rise and come upon them, but by necessity they hastened to him and fought with him. They mastered him, they detained him. They bound him with their body and their limbs, they overcame his death and his fire and his darkness.

[The] second time that they wept is [when the]ir father, the First Man, [ascend]ed from the [abyss] of darkness and left them behind; that is the time when he stripped [them off] and left them below. Indeed, when th[ey] s[aw] how the First Man had risen out of the abyss and [l]eft them behind, and that they were abandoned in the enmit[y, th]ey wept and were sore of heart. Still, what could they do, wishing [to subject] their heart to every affliction. They [remained b]ehind and grew [s]ick under the pressure of the weighty burden of all the works, until the end time.

[The] third time that they wept is when the Living Spirit stripped off the three garments of activity, placing them beneath all things. He gave them a sign to lift their heads and rise to the heights from that place; and to pass and journey through all the earths until they should reach the land of tranquilli[t]y and peace, the place of rest prepared for them. So, when they had seen him, that he had separated himself from them, while they themselves remained behind after him and had not ascended; at that moment when they stayed behind these three garments wept. After their crying, they turned their [hear]t to all the heights that were concealed from them, and were of one mind. For [they would] soar up and come to the heights; and pass over all things until the time that was ordained for them all [and be gathered up] at the end of the worlds.

[The f]ourth time when they will weep is when the [S]tatue will be taken up on the last day, and they will weep [for] the souls of the liars and blasphemers; for they may give [no help to them] because their limbs have been severed [from the bonds] of the darkness. And also [th]ose souls, when the Statue will go up and th]ey are left alo[n]e, they will weep in that they will rema[in] behind in affliction for ever. For they wi[ll be cut off] and separated from the Last Statue. An[d it is] a necessity to take these souls who are ready for loss as retribution for the deeds that they have done. They go i[n to] this [darkne]ss and are bound with the darkness; just as they desired it and loved it, and placed their treasure with it. At that very moment, when the Last Statue rises up, the[y wi]ll weep. And then they will scream out loud because they will be severed from the company of this great Statue. And they remain behind for ever. This great weeping [before the rulers] is terrible, it occurs in front of the souls and [the powers] who are ready for loss in accordance with their deeds. And they [will] weep with that crying, they will never be silent; because they will not attain rest from this time on.

So, they too are the garments of these elements. This fourth time of weeping is heart-rending for them. It is much worse for them than these other three times of weeping before. This fourth time the weeping is not for themselves. Rather they weep and are heartsore for these soul[s] who will be cut off from peace, because rest will not come about for them, to allow them to rest from torment for ever.
